verdict.rationale: Amplitude's SDK docs describe official SDKs sharing one API surface across web, mobile, server, and game engines. The integrations directory names specific Flutter and React Native SDKs, and an HTTP V2 endpoint is documented for server-side sending. Missing for 10: an explicit list of the major backend/native languages covered (e.g., which server languages, native iOS/Android), and independent hands-on corroboration of SDK coverage and quality.

support.subject: As a developer, I can send events from web, mobile, and backend apps through official SDKs for the major languages and platforms

citations.quote: Use the same API surface across web, mobile, server, and game engines.
Every SDK shares the same identity, event, and consent model, so a user instrumented once is understood everywhere.
An SDK that contains the necessary API's to use Amplitude effectively in a React Native application.
Send data directly from your server to the HTTP V2 endpoint.
The wizard detects your framework, installs the right SDK, adds your API key, and fires a test event.
